:::{#rem-empirical-information-opg}
#### The empirical information as an outer product of gradients

Each term $\score_\iobs \tp{\score_\iobs}$ of the [empirical information matrix](#def-empirical-information)
is the [self outer product](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-inner-products.html#def-self-outer-product)
of the $i$th [observation](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-observation)'s [score](#def-score).
At a [maximum likelihood estimate](#def-mle) that solves the [score equation](#def-score-equation),
the score $\score$ of the whole [sample](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample)
is the [zero vector](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-zero-vector),
so the second term of the empirical information is the [zero matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-zero-matrix),
and the empirical information is the [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) of these self outer products.
Econometrics sources call this sum the [outer product](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-inner-products.html#def-outer-product)
of [gradients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/vector-calculus.html#def-vector-derivative),
and the Berndt-Hall-Hall-Hausman (BHHH) algorithm uses it in place of the [observed information](#def-oinf) in each Newton-Raphson step
[@wikipedia_bhhh].

:::
